original_finding.description: Static reasoning, not executed. checked_cache (compaction_heads.rs:373-418) compares every cached author's stored DeviceRecord with the CURRENT first verified record from commit::device_registry. That registry takes the first object in numeric-HLC/author total order and first op order (commit.rs:2305-2333, order_key commit.rs:326). checked_cache now runs on every exactly-next n>1 receipt (receive -> hlc_not_above_previous, commit.rs:2492), on every deferred release (commit.rs:2245), on every local author_commit (membership.rs:356), on the standalone and TeamSync authorized fact signing paths (membership.rs:446, sync.rs:6490), and the same comparison runs in prepare (compaction_heads.rs:295). The fingerprint is SHA-256(sign_pub) only (identity.rs:125). DeviceRecord::verify checks only the self-signature over agree_pub (identity.rs:105-118). So a holder of cached author Y's signing key can mint a different self-verifying full record Y' (a new agree_pub) under the same fingerprint. Receipt does not stop Y' from becoming the registry's first record. The commit of a newly admitted device X at seq 1 gets no HLC predecessor check (cached_hlc_not_above_previous returns false for seq<=1). Past wall clocks are never refused. Fold-skipped and removed authors still pass the registry-based receipt. Concrete sequence: a compaction has cached Y's head. Y authors Y:n with member.add(X), which receipt accepts even if fold skips it as not_admin. X:1 has HLC 1-0000, sorts first, and carries member.add(Y'). From then on, checked_cache returns team_compaction_head_invalid for EVERY author's exactly-next receipt (handle_commit propagates the error and ends the session receive loop, sync.rs:7700-7705). advance_env then fails on each poll tick while a due next deferred commit exists (sync.rs:8561), so dial and VECTOR stop for that environment. Every local author_commit and authorized fact fails, including the admin's member.remove commit and member_removed fact against the attacker, and compaction is refused for good. The integration test compaction_heads_01_later_conflicting_record_cannot_override_and_earlier_arrival_refuses (tests/team_compaction_heads.rs:1593-1700) sets up exactly this earlier-arrival case, with X already removed. It asserts compaction refusal and a local error on Y's own next receipt, but it does not cover receipt by other authors, deferred release, local commits, removal or fact signing. The Astra decision chose 'earlier conflicting arrival => invalid/no overwrite'. Its residual table, however, analyses only compaction refusal and LOCAL corruption, not an insider-triggered, environment-wide halt of receipt and signing that also blocks remediation. Before this change (04c7d22) the same conflict could at most refuse compaction. The fix widened the blast radius. Availability only: I found no secret, plaintext or authority exposure, and no data loss or unlink. Personal vault and ordinary reads stay usable. The only recovery is deleting compaction_heads.json by hand (back to legacy absence, after which compaction stays unavailable for pruned idle heads), and no procedure for that is defined.
original_finding.required_change: Escalate to Astra for a bounded decision. Do not silently relax the rules. Options: (a) at receipt (a protected change), refuse or quarantine any env.init/member.add announcement whose fingerprint already has a different full verified record in the retained registry, so the first record is immutable once established. This also needs a decision for an earlier-sorted announcement of an identical or different record. (b) Keep the strict cache-vs-registry equality as a compaction-only refusal. At receipt and signing, validate cached heads against the cached record plus the existence of an equal verified retained announcement for that fingerprint, not against the current first one. The cache still grants no membership. (c) Explicitly accept and document the environment-wide halt with a defined, authority-free operator outcome. Whatever is chosen, add real-path tests: compact with Y cached; a single insider (Y alone, including the Y-adds-X variant and the variant where Y is already removed) introduces an earlier-sorted Y'; then assert literal outcomes for another author's next receipt via receive_commit and handle_commit, deferred release, owner author_commit (data and member.remove of Y), member_removed and secret_deleted facts, and compaction, with exact rejected/deferred/audit inventories and preserved originals.

original_finding.description: Static reasoning, not executed. prepare() resolves each required author's public DeviceRecord only from identity_document.members, which compact builds with the fact-free fold::fold over live commits (sync.rs:9257). Receipt admits commits using commit.rs device_registry (commit.rs:2263-2290). That registry takes the device of EVERY verified env.init/member.add op, whether or not fold accepted the op. fold computes FoldResult.vector over every ordered commit, including skipped ones (fold.rs:2048-2056). Consider an author Y whose member.add was skipped by fold: for example a non-admin author (op_member_add returns not_admin, fold.rs:990-992), or a legitimate race where the adding admin's role was removed earlier in HLC order. Y's own signed commits are accepted and stored and enter snapshot.vector. They then become a required slot, local_record(Y) returns team_compaction_head_unavailable, and every later compact of the environment refuses. Before this change those commits would simply have been compacted. Y cannot be removed from the vector and its member.add can never be pruned, so the refusal has no recovery path. It is fail-closed (no data loss, no unlink), but it is a permanent compaction denial that any member able to author commits can trigger, and an ordinary concurrent role change can trigger it by accident. No test covers a stored author outside the fold member map.
original_finding.required_change: Decide and implement one bounded semantics inside the allowed files. Recommended: source signature-verification material for required heads with the same rule receipt used. Take the first self-verifying env.init owner_device/member.add device with a matching fingerprint from the retained live commits, re-implemented privately in compaction_heads.rs because commit.rs is protected. Still require record.verify(), fingerprint==author, full-record equality for cached slots and verify_commit. State in a comment that this is public signature material, not membership authority. Alternatively, keep such authors' commits live and document why they are not cut evidence. Either way, add a real-compactor test: a non-admin member.add of Y, then Y's commit, all older than the age cutoff, with literal expected slot/cache/deletion outcomes. Also add the reopen/second-compact case.

original_finding.description: Static reasoning, not executed. The new rule refuses when a higher required slot's HLC is <= the cached head's HLC (compaction_heads.rs:320-325). Receipt enforces per-author HLC monotonicity only against the immediately previous sequence when the store still holds it: hlc_not_above_previous returns false when get(author, seq-1) is None (commit.rs:2149-2156). The protected receipt path never consults the cache. After a compaction deletes author A's data head n-1, which is now only in the cache, a commit A:n with any HLC <= the deleted head's HLC passes receipt, the past-wall check and the store. It is not future-skewed, so no deferral occurs. Once A:n is older than COMPACT_MIN_AGE_MS and is the required slot, prepare returns team_compaction_head_invalid on every attempt. The refusal clears only if A later produces a higher, monotone, aged head; if A is idle or removed it never clears. The cache therefore imposes an invariant that the existing admission path does not guarantee after compaction. A malicious or clock-reset member device can turn that gap into a persistent compaction denial. It is fail-closed (no data loss), but no test exercises a regressed HLC arriving through real receipt after compaction; the unit test only constructs prepare() inputs directly.
original_finding.required_change: Escalate to the coordinator/Astra for a bounded decision, because closing this at admission needs protected commit.rs/sync receipt changes; that is a STOP under the task. Options: (a) a separately scoped change so receipt compares seq n against the cached head when seq n-1 is absent (fail closed); (b) keep the refusal but document it as a known permanent-refusal mode with a defined, authority-free operator outcome. Do not silently drop the old evidence. Add a real-path test that compacts, receives A:n with a regressed old HLC through receive_commit, ages it, then compacts, and asserts the literal decided outcome.

original_finding.description: Static reasoning, not executed. sync_directories requires symlink_metadata(current).is_dir() for every directory from the child up to and including StateDir.path. Existing StateDir::require uses is_dir(), which follows symlinks, so a symlinked state root (or a symlinked team/ or team/{env} directory) is otherwise accepted. With such a layout, every compaction fails with team_compaction_head_persist_failed. The failure comes only after fold::save_snapshot and save_snapshot_record have already written new metadata (sync.rs:9262-9285). It is fail-closed (no unlink), but compaction becomes permanently unavailable for that layout, and the refusal is not a prospective check made before mutation. check_snapshot likewise uses the symlink-following read_json without the regular-file check that read_record applies.
original_finding.required_change: Before any snapshot/record write, validate the durability-barrier preconditions (directory chain type and containment). Then either explicitly and fixed-reason refuse a symlinked root/ancestor before mutation, documented as unsupported, or canonicalize StateDir.path once and then require no symlinks below it. Apply the same regular-file check to the snapshot readback. Add a test with a symlinked state root or team directory that asserts the decided outcome and that no new snapshot/record/cache files exist.
